concept.name: Mental stop
concept.definition: A stop-loss level held in the trader's mind rather than placed as an order with the broker: the trader commits to exit manually if price reaches the level. It preserves flexibility and avoids order visibility but depends entirely on real-time discipline under stress.
concept.intuition: A mental stop is a promise to yourself; the market will test exactly your willingness to keep it.
concept.mechanics: The invalidation level is defined at entry but no resting order is working; when price trades there, the trader must execute the exit manually, which introduces hesitation risk, delay slippage, and the temptation to renegotiate. It is the discretionary counterpart of the hard stop, which is an actual stop or stop-limit order resting at the venue.
concept.failure_modes: It fails precisely when needed most: fast markets, news spikes, and tilt states, where the trader freezes, moves the level, or averages down instead. Without a working order, gaps and connectivity failures leave the position unprotected.
concept.misconceptions: Mental stops are not 'more professional'; they are appropriate mainly for experienced traders in liquid markets who watch the position continuously. Honoring a mental stop nine times out of ten still leaves the tenth - often the catastrophic one.
concept.example: Long from 50 with a mental stop at 48.50; a surprise headline dumps the stock through the level in seconds and the trader, hesitating, exits at 47.90 - triple the planned slippage.
